children: Bharti Airtel shares snapped a three-session gaining streak on Monday, falling over 3 per cent amid profit booking.
The shares settled at Rs 1,830.20 apiece on the NSE, down 3.33 per cent.
The stock had gained more than 3 per cent in the previous three sessions.
Pravesh Gour, Senior Technical Analyst at Swastika Investmart, said Bharti Airtel has given back a significant portion of its recent recovery, with the stock falling more than 3 per cent.
"The chart shows the stock trading around Rs 1,832, below its short- and medium-term moving averages, indicating that the near-term trend has weakened," Gour said.
The 9-day and 20-day averages have turned lower, while the stock remains below the 50-, 100- and 200-day averages, keeping the broader technical structure under pressure, he said.
The immediate support zone is around Rs 1,800-1,775. A decisive break below Rs 1,775 could increase selling pressure towards the stock's 52-week low area of around Rs 1,745.

On the upside, Rs 1,855-1,875 is the first resistance zone, followed by Rs 1,900-1,930. A sustained move above Rs 1,900 would improve the short-term setup and could signal that the recent decline was only a correction, Gour said.

Momentum indicators also remain cautious. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is around the mid-40s, indicating weakening momentum but not an oversold condition. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains below the zero line, although the histogram and lines show early signs of stabilisation.
"The stock does not yet show a strong momentum-based reversal signal," Gour said.

For existing holders, the chart currently supports a hold-with-risk-control approach, provided the Rs 1,775-1,800 zone holds, he said. For a fresh entry, Gour said it may be preferable to wait for either a strong reversal from this support zone or a sustained move back above Rs 1,900.
A break below Rs 1,775 would materially weaken the setup, he said.

Vishnu Kant Upadhyay, AVP, Research, Master Capital Services Ltd, said Bharti Airtel continues to hold above its ascending trendline despite the recent pullback, with the Rs 1,800-1,830 zone acting as a buying area.
"However, the stock has failed to reclaim its 100-day and 200-day EMAs near Rs 1,900, from where the recent decline emerged," Upadhyay said.
The stock is now close to its trendline support, which has provided buying opportunities in the past, he said.
"The technical structure supports holding the stock, while the current correction can be used to accumulate near support. Fresh buying should be considered cautiously," Upadhyay said.
